findings.title: Constructor null-check uses wrong argument for rawTokenId
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic
Shortcut-collision validation does not catch duplicate shortcuts
Unchecked cast to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory in postInit
findings.body: `postInit` performs `(OAuth2GrantTypeFactory) factory1` for every factory returned by `getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)`. The stream type only guarantees `ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType>`, not `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`. Any third-party extension that registers an `OAuth2GrantType` without implementing `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` will cause a `ClassCastException` at server startup. Either filter on `instanceof OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` or guarantee the relationship contractually.

findings.title: Adding abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a default implementation. Although the interface lives in `server-spi-private`, external grant-type extensions routinely implement it (every Keycloak extension that adds a custom grant does so). Adding a non-default method is a compile-time breaking change for any such extension and a runtime ClassCastException/NoSuchMethodError for those loaded by reflection before recompilation. Consider providing a default (e.g. returning the first two characters of `getId()`, or `UNKNOWN`) so that existing custom factories keep working.

findings.title: Removed Context copy constructor
findings.body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor that was previously on `OAuth2GrantType.Context` is deleted. The diff message is misleading - the constructor was not just unused inside these files, but is part of a private SPI that custom grant extensions may rely on (e.g. to clone context to a sub-task or to wrap it for retries). The deleted constructor also closes the door on the previously available pattern of reusing one `Context`. Either keep it, deprecate it, or document clearly that this SPI is consumed by external extensions.

findings.title: getShouldUseLightweightToken widened from package-private to public
findings.body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken` is changed from package-private to `public static`. This is required for the new encoder to reach it, but it is also expanding the public surface of an unrelated class in ways not strictly required by the PR (a small package-private helper on a wrapper class would have been enough). Either keep it package-private and move the lightweight-token resolution into `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper` itself, or accept the API widening and document it.

findings.title: Test relies on NPE rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: `testIncorrectGrantType` exercises the unknown-shortcut path (`ac` is not in the manually populated map) but never calls `factory.postInit(...)`, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` ends up dereferencing the null `sessionFactory` and throws NullPointerException, which is then swallowed by the `catch (RuntimeException)` clause. The test passes only because NPE happens to extend `RuntimeException`. The test should populate the maps explicitly (as it already does), or use `assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...)` once the method is fixed to throw a documented exception, instead of implicitly relying on a side-effect NPE.

findings.title: No integration coverage for the encoded access-token format
findings.body: The PR introduces a new on-the-wire format for `jti` (e.g. `onrtrt:<uuid>`) and changes every test helper that asserts on `Details.TOKEN_ID`. There is no integration test that round-trips through `createClientAccessToken` -> JWT signing -> token manager decode to confirm that `TokenManager` and the introspection / UMA / account endpoints all still recognise tokens minted under the new format. Because the matching helper in `AssertEvents` is also broken, the existing tests cannot act as a safety net for this either. At least one integration test exercising a token-end-to-end (login + introspection + refresh) is needed.

findings.title: Stale comment about clientSession note remains
findings.body: The diff `sessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` is added next to the unchanged `clientSession.setNote(VC_ISSUANCE_FLOW, ...)`. There is no comment explaining why both are needed (the note stores the VC flow marker, the attribute stores the grant type for the encoder). The PR would benefit from a single-line comment indicating the dual-purpose nature of these two assignments so the next reader does not delete the attribute thinking it duplicates the note.

findings.title: Refresh path double-lookups the map
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType` first does `grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType)`, and if null, then potentially recomputes the entry and then does a second `grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType)`. For an unknown grant type this is two map lookups; for a known one it's also two if you count the assignment on line 116. Minor, but more importantly the asynchronous refresh logic in `getGrantTypeByShortcut` walks the entire `OAuth2GrantType` factory stream every time the cached map misses - on a server with many grant types this is wasteful, especially as `findFirst` after `filter` could short-circuit earlier. Consider caching the per-shortcut lookup result the first time it is computed.
